messages.text: Rybakina withdraws from Pan Pacific Open with injury

metadata.summary: World No 1 Elena Rybakina has withdrawn injured against Leylah Fernandez in the Pan Pacific Open to exit the tournament at the quarter-final stage.
metadata.content: Pan Pacific Open: Elena Rybakina withdraws from Pan Pacific Open with injury just one day after securing year-end No 1 ranking | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Pan Pacific Open: Elena Rybakina withdraws from Pan Pacific Open with injury just one day after securing year-end No 1 ranking World No 1 Elena Rybakina has withdrawn injured against Leylah Fernandez in the Pan Pacific Open; watch the WTA and ATP Tours live on Sky Sports, with action from Vienna and Osaka headlining throughout this week Friday 30 October 2026 07:43, UK Image: Elena Rybakina withdrew from her match against Leylah Fernandez World No 1 Elena Rybakina has withdrawn injured against Leylah Fernandez in the Pan Pacific Open to exit the tournament at the quarter-final stage. The Kazakh player withdrew from the match before a point was played, giving the Canadian Fernandez safe passage into the last four in Osaka, where she will play Kamilla Rakhimova for a place in the final. "I just wanted to say thank you so much for coming today, but unfortunately I won't be able to play," the 27-year-old said on-court. messages.text: Vilips takes first-round lead at Mexico Open

metadata.summary: Karl Vilips used two long birdie streaks to take the first-round lead Thursday in the Mexico Open, the first of two straight PGA Tour events in the country.
metadata.content: Mexico Open: Karl Vilips shoots 62 to take the first-round lead with Marco Penge two shots back | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mexico Open: Karl Vilips shoots 62 to take the first-round lead with Marco Penge two shots back England's Marco Penge was two shots off leader Karl Vilips after round one of the Mexico Open, while US Open champion Wyndham Clark shot a 69 as the only top 10 player in the field; watch live coverage of round two from 8pm on Sky Sports Golf on Friday Friday 30 October 2026 07:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first round of the Mexican Open Karl Vilips used two long birdie streaks to take the first-round lead Thursday in the Mexico Open, the first of two straight PGA Tour events in the country. Vilips shot a nine-under 62 in the afternoon round on the Vidanta Vallarta layout, making five straight birdies on Nos. 11-15 on his opening nine and finishing with four in a row. In between, he had another birdie and a bogey. The 25-year-old Australian pointed to his driver. "Had it on a string for the first nine," Vilips said. "Got a little loose in the middle and got it back on course toward the end of the round. It was lift, clean and place today so being in the fairway was a must for me and I took advantage of those drives that I hit." messages.text: Love leads Packers past Panthers in vital win

metadata.summary: Jordan Love threw three touchdown passes, Josh Jacobs scored twice and the Green Bay Packers withstood three turnovers and the Carolina Panthers' late comeback attempt to win 27-19 at Lambeau Field.
metadata.content: Carolina Panthers 19-27 Green Bay Packers: Jordan Love throws three touchdown passes in vital win | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Carolina Panthers 19-27 Green Bay Packers: Jordan Love throws three touchdown passes in vital win The Green Bay Packers beat the Carolina Panthers 27-19 at Lambeau Field; Jordan Love threw three touchdowns and Christian Watson returned to the game after going to the hospital; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs Friday 30 October 2026 06:40, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Carolina Panthers against the Green Bay Packers from Week 8 of the NFL season Jordan Love threw three touchdown passes, Josh Jacobs scored twice and the Green Bay Packers withstood three turnovers and the Carolina Panthers' late comeback attempt to win 27-19 at Lambeau Field. Love went 30 of 41 for 288 yards with touchdown passes to Tucker Kraft, Matthew Golden and Jacobs plus an interception. Although Jacobs rushed for only 39 yards on 21 carries against the NFL's lowest-ranked run defense, he scored on a 4-yard catch and 1-yard run. That was more than enough for the Packers on a night when they sacked Bryce Young six times. Green Bay hasn't allowed any of its last five opponents to exceed 20 points. metadata.summary: Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso has doubled down on his criticism of "low level" Formula 1 drivers who have a "lack of talent" following his collision with Williams' Alex Albon in Austin.

Albon tried to overtake Alonso for 12th place into the Turn 11 hairpin on the opening lap of the United States Grand Prix, but went into the side of the Aston Martin driver, damaging both cars. Neither driver received a penalty and both were able to continue with Alonso finishing 16th and Albon in 17th in Austin. messages.text: England crash out of World Cup as Ropati leads Samoa to victory

metadata.summary: England have crashed out of the Women’s Rugby League World Cup after a 24-6 defeat to Samoa in Wollongong.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: England lose 24-6 to Samoa and make group-stage exit from women's tournament | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Rugby League World Cup: England lose 24-6 to Samoa and make group-stage exit from women's tournament Friday 30 October 2026 08:32, UK Image: England are out of the Women's Rugby League World Cup after defeat to Samoa England have crashed out of the Women’s Rugby League World Cup after a 24-6 defeat to Samoa in Wollongong. Stuart Barrow's side needed victory to secure a top-two finish in Group A and qualify for a third consecutive World Cup semi-final, only to see their campaign ended by a second successive loss. Freedom Crichton Ropati scored a first-half hat-trick as Samoa raced into a 12-0 lead at the break, with Mercedez Taulelei-Siala extending the Pacific islanders' advantage early in the second half.
